one-check-per-line.why: all 4 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 4

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

words-only.why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Checks 1, 2 and 4 stay within their words. Check 1 runs functional clamp cases. Check 2 tests that RangeError is thrown when lo > hi. Check 4 needs exit 0 and fail 0. Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its PASS condition needs "the script prints missing: none", and the script fails any exported function unless a markdown heading matches '^#+\s*name\s*\('. The expect line only says "README.md documents every function math.js exports". It doesn't require headings. A README that documents subtract in a bullet list or a table would meet the words but FAIL this check. That format rule belongs under Advisory, not in a PASS/FAIL condition.

runs-as-written.why: The builder brief's commands work: `npm test` maps to "node --test", and math.js, README.md and test/math.test.js all exist. Verifier Checks 1, 2 and 4 are valid shell and JavaScript. Check 3 is not. Its script sits inside bash double quotes, where `\\` becomes `\`. So the JavaScript gets the string literals '^#+\s*' and '\s*\(', and in a JS string `\s` is just `s` and `\(` is just `(`. The regex built is therefore "^#+s*adds*(". That has an unterminated group, so `new RegExp` throws a SyntaxError. The check crashes instead of testing README headings, which means it does not run as written.

catches-traps.why: I checked all three must_catch items, and the briefs handle each one. (1) Builder step 3 tells the builder to add a "### subtract(a, b)" entry "(it is currently missing)" as well as a "### clamp(x, lo, hi)" entry, and to make sure every name in module.exports has a heading. (2) Verifier Check 3 reads the function list from math.js's exports at the PR head. It then has the verifier confirm "at least add, subtract, multiply, clamp" each have a README entry. It FAILs if any exported function lacks one, and notes that "subtract was previously undocumented". (3) Verifier Check 2 calls clamp with lo > hi in four cases. It FAILs on "!(e instanceof RangeError)" or if the call returns normally, so a generic error does not pass.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked each verifier check against the two must_not items. Item 1 holds: Check 3 lists every exported function, and its FAIL condition names subtract, so a README that documents clamp but not subtract fails. Checks 1, 2 and 4 hold too: Check 1 tests values, Check 2 only needs `instanceof RangeError` with no message match, and Check 4 needs exit 0 with no failing tests. Item 2 is broken in Check 3. Its script only counts a function as documented if README.md has a markdown heading matching `'^#+\\s*'+n+'\\s*\\('`, and PASS needs "missing: none". A README that documents every export some other way, such as in a table, a bullet list or prose, would FAIL. The expect line only says README.md "documents every function math.js exports", so this condition requires a specific README layout and is stricter than its line.
